headline: KINROSS DRILLS GOLD IN EVERY HOLE AT BTU'S DIXIE HALO — UP TO 6 G/T AU PLUS 24.55M AT 0.63% COPPER-SILVER IN TNT AREA
snippet: Kinross encountered gold mineralization in all eight diamond drill holes (4,528.5m total) in the TNT area of BTU Metals Corp.'s (TSX-V: BTU) Dixie Halo project in Ontario — grades ranging from below 1 g/t to 6 g/t Au — with copper-silver also intersected in hole BTU-26-15 at 24.55m grading 0.626% Cu and 12.61 g/t Ag, including a 0.4m sub-interval at 8.41% Cu and 116 g/t Ag. Kinross continues drilling as it works toward earning a 70% interest in the Dixie Halo project under its existing option agreement.

headline: COPPER SETS ALL-TIME RECORD $14,694/T BEFORE WHITE HOUSE TARIFF BLINK — FCX SINKS 8%, TECK 7%, FIRST WEEKLY LOSS SINCE JUNE
snippet: Copper reached an all-time LME high of US$14,694 per tonne on September 8 — driven by a Codelco El Teniente output decline of 27% in the first five months of 2026 and surging downstream Chinese demand — before Reuters reported the White House was reconsidering whether to impose tariffs on refined copper ahead of November midterms, sending Comex futures down 4.4% and Freeport-McMoRan shares down 8.2% to close Friday's week as copper's first losing week since June.

headline: CHINA'S RARE EARTH SUSPENSION EXPIRES NOVEMBER 10 — THREE SCENARIOS THAT COULD PUT $6.5T IN DOWNSTREAM PRODUCTION AT RISK
snippet: China's 12-month suspension of its October 2025 expanded rare earth export controls lapses November 10, 2026, and the IEA estimates full reimposition could endanger $6.5 trillion in global downstream production across automotive, defence, and energy sectors. Three policy outcomes are in play: an extension of the suspension, selective reinstatement targeting specific heavy rare earth elements, or full reimposition including extraterritorial provisions. April 2025 case-by-case export licences on seven medium and heavy rare earths — terbium, dysprosium, samarium, gadolinium, lutetium, scandium, and yttrium — remain in force regardless of November's outcome.

headline: STANMORE SEALS $105M MORANBAH SOUTH BUY — 724MT PREMIUM HARD COKING COAL BOLTS ON TO QUEENSLAND OPERATIONS
snippet: Stanmore Resources (ASX: SMR) has agreed to acquire 100% of the Moranbah South metallurgical coal tenements in Queensland's Bowen Basin from Exxaro Resources for US$105 million, adding 724 million tonnes of measured and indicated resources in the Goonyella Middle Seam — expected to be premium hard coking coal quality — adjacent to its existing Eagle Downs and Isaac Plains Complex operations. Completion is targeted before end of Q4 2026, subject to FIRB and ACCC approval.

headline: ANGLO-TECK'S $54B CLOSE WINDOW JUST OPENED — SOUTH KOREA CLEARED, ONLY CHINA'S SAMR STANDS BETWEEN DEAL AND A TOP-5 COPPER GIANT
snippet: Anglo American and Teck Resources have cleared every major regulatory hurdle except China's SAMR anti-monopoly review for their $54 billion merger of equals — a deal that would create a top-5 global copper producer headquartered in Vancouver with approximately 15% of global copper mine output. South Korea's approval was confirmed in Q2 2026; CEO Duncan Wanblad confirmed active SAMR engagement with the closing window running September 2026 to March 2027. China's review carries strategic weight as the world's largest copper consumer absorbing roughly half of annual global refined output.

headline: THE HIKE IS PRICED IN — SILVER'S SPECULATIVE POSITIONING ISN'T, AND THE ASYMMETRIC FOMC TRADE IS LONG SILVER AT $63
snippet: With silver at $63.22 and speculative net-long positioning still well below June highs despite August's 14.9% outperformance of gold, GoldSilver's September analysis argues that a Fed hold — currently below 15% probability — would deliver an asymmetric silver rally while the expected hike is already embedded in the price. Silver fell four times as steeply as gold on September 11's selloff, signalling institutional position flushing rather than a structural shift; the sixth consecutive annual supply deficit at 46.3 million ounces and China's January export licensing have not changed the structural backdrop.

headline: LITHIUM DEMAND SURGES 45% THROUGH MAY — BATTERY STORAGE OVERTAKES EVS AS DRIVER WITH 200,000T LCE DEFICIT LOOMING IN Q4
snippet: Albemarle's latest market data shows global lithium consumption rose 45% year-over-year through May 2026, with stationary battery storage — now approximately 20% of total global battery demand — surpassing EVs as the primary incremental driver, fuelled by AI data centre power requirements and grid reliability upgrades. Supply delays position the market for a 200,000–400,000 metric tonne LCE deficit by Q4 2026 (15–25% of global demand), though analyst estimates range widely from Morgan Stanley's 80,000 tonnes to UBS's 22,000 tonnes depending on project ramp assumptions.

headline: GOLD-SILVER RATIO'S 12-POINT SWING IN 12 WEEKS — AT 66.3, WHAT THE 61.7-TO-70.4-AND-BACK ROUND TRIP SIGNALS FOR RETAIL POSITIONING
snippet: The gold-silver ratio has completed an unusual 12-point round trip — from 61.7 in late June to 70.4 in mid-August and back to 66.3 by mid-September — a volatility range far outside its historical norm for a three-month window. The analysis argues this is an institutional positioning signal: silver's smaller float means the same dollar of buying moves it proportionally more than gold, producing amplified swings that retail investors interpret as fundamental divergence when it is mostly market structure. At 66.3, silver remains historically cheap relative to gold when measured against the 2011–2026 average of 78.

headline: GOLD MINING STOCKS VS. BULLION: THE 3–5X LEVERAGE MATH MOST RETAIL INVESTORS GET WRONG AT $4,285 GOLD
snippet: With gold above $4,200 and industry-wide AISC below $2,000 per ounce, mining equities offer theoretical operating leverage of 3–5x to a gold price move — but GoldSilver's September analysis explains why the leverage math breaks down when reserve depletion, equity dilution, geopolitical risk, and balance-sheet debt are included. The piece maps out correct AISC-based margin calculations and explains why retail investors consistently overweight single-asset juniors on leverage assumptions that apply only to steady-state producers with controlled permitting exposure.

headline: CODELCO EL TENIENTE -27% COPPER OUTPUT PLUS FREEPORT DECLINE: THE SUPPLY SHOCK THAT CREATED SEPTEMBER'S $14,694 RECORD
snippet: Codelco's El Teniente — the world's largest underground copper mine — produced 27% less copper in the first five months of 2026 than a year earlier after its Andes Norte expansion was suspended August 4 on seismic risk grounds, contributing to a 1.1% decline in global copper output in H1 2026 per the International Copper Study Group. Combined with Freeport-McMoRan posting double-digit production declines, the structural supply tightening created the conditions for copper's all-time record of $14,694 per tonne on September 8 before the tariff reversal triggered a sharp correction.
